=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:171-187 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: `prepare_untrusted_poller_runtime` copies trusted helper scripts from the model-writable checkout, allowing a persistent runner to install and execute a model-modified trusted Git writer, commit/push boundary, or sandbox script on a later poller invocation.
  WHY: On persistent/self-hosted runners, the next poller tick can copy and execute a compromised worktree version; x-ai_grok-4_20 reports this staging issue as fixed.

- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:5716-5752; scripts/security_audit.sh:1635-1676 | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: Waiver revalidation relies on causal fingerprints and ancestor verification without preserving the old file-diff and guard-deletion checks, so changes outside the reverse-call scope can leave a waiver suppressing a newly exploitable sink.
  WHY: New callers, cross-file authorization changes, or decorators outside the four-depth causal scope may not alter the fingerprint or trigger `causal_scope_changed_files`.

- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:8761-8836 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: When unresolved conflict paths remain after the resolver runs, execution falls through to the generic failure warning and duplicate cleanup instead of returning or branching separately.
  WHY: Operators receive contradictory diagnostics for one failure and cannot distinguish an unresolved resolver result from a failed judge execution; the safety behavior remains correct.

- .github/workflows/implement.yml:4481-4496 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The push block reads `refs/remotes/origin/${TARGET_BRANCH}` without fetching current remote state before computing `expected_remote_head`.
  WHY: After sibling changes advance the integration branch during a long run, `trusted_git_write.sh` can reject an otherwise additive push because its `ls-remote` value differs from the stale tracking ref.

- scripts/trusted_git_write.sh:147 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The credential fallback chain accepts `${GITHUB_TOKEN:-}` in addition to `${GH_TOKEN:-}` and `${GH_PAT:-}`.
  WHY: A future caller that omits the intended credential wiring could silently push with the restricted Actions token, contrary to the intended broad-PAT boundary.

- scripts/trusted_git_write.sh:173-184 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: A third-party can theoretically push the same SHA between `ls-remote` and `git push`, allowing the lease to match and the push to overwrite that third-party commit.
  WHY: The documented exact remote-head validation has a time-of-check-to-time-of-use window, although the required coincidental force-push is highly unlikely.

- scripts/security_audit_causality.py:289-298 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: `OSError`, `SyntaxError`, `UnicodeError`, and `ValueError` are collapsed into the same `causal_scope_status: "indeterminate"` payload without surfacing the diagnostic reason.
  WHY: Operators cannot distinguish transient Git errors from permanent parse failures while security findings remain blocking.

- scripts/security_audit_causality.py:142-162 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: `_snapshot` invokes `git show <ref>:<file>` for every Python file at both refs for each finding, making the capped work proportional to findings multiplied by repository size.
  WHY: A 500-file repository with 20 findings can produce approximately 20,000 subprocess calls per audit cycle and dominate wall-clock time.

- scripts/untrusted_process_sandbox.sh:230-241 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: `UNTRUSTED_PROCESS_SANDBOX_TEST_MODE=1` bypasses every systemd-run network and filesystem isolation property.
  WHY: An operator enabling the test mode on a production runner removes all security boundaries without a warning, refusal guard, or bypass documentation.

- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:4470-4498 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The secretless-container validation step runs the entire pytest suite without a selector, marker filter, or conftest override inside a networkless read-only container.
  WHY: Network-dependent, writable-tree, external-service, or environment-dependent tests fail regardless of editor correctness, withholding changes and potentially causing an unrecoverable retry loop.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
